exposure: adult attachment dimensions (perceived availability, feared loss, separation protest, angry withdrawal, compulsive careseeking)
outcome: subjective birth experience (overall, perceived control, perceived social support, satisfaction)
cohort: The study included 257 mothers with a mean age of 30.5 years (61% primiparas, 26% delivered by caesarean) who participated in an online survey 4 days to 12 months after giving birth.
finding: The study found direct effects from mothers' adult attachment dimensions to their subjective birth experiences.
mod_finding: Interactions emerged for mode of delivery, along with parity, influencing overall subjective birth experience, perceived control, perceived social support, and satisfaction.
